title: fix(plugin-hono-server)!: the CORS default admits no cross-origin caller, and '*' with credentials is refused at boot
body:
Fixes #24738
Clause-②: no (narrowing)

## What changes

The CORS middleware that `HonoServerPlugin` (the server `os serve`, `os dev` and `os start` mount) installs by default now admits only the origins it is told about. The governing text is `docs/HARDENING.md` § CORS: "Do **not** use `origin: '*'` with `credentials: true`", and the go-live checklist's "CORS origin list is explicit, not `*`".

- **Old default.** With no origin list configured (no `cors.origins` option, no `OS_CORS_ORIGIN`), every origin was admitted for credentialed cross-origin requests. A configured `'*'` with credentials on was accepted and answered the same way.
- **New default.** With no list, no cross-origin caller is admitted. A loopback origin (`localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `[::1]`, any port) is admitted on a development boot only: `NODE_ENV` exactly `development`, read through `isDevelopmentBoot` from `@objectstack/core`, the same reading the auth secret's development fallback uses.
- **`'*'` with credentials** is refused in `init()`. `kernel.bootstrap()` rethrows an `init()` throw, so the boot fails, and the message names both remedies (`OS_CORS_ORIGIN`, `OS_CORS_CREDENTIALS=false`). This is the precedent of `@objectstack/plugin-dev`'s production guard (`assertNotProduction`, ADR-0115 D6), which refuses the same way from `init()`. Triage leaned to a loud refusal, and the transport has no non-credentialed fallback that would keep the operator's intent.

Docs now state the default as it is: `docs/HARDENING.md` § CORS only, the CORS rows of `environment-variables.mdx`, one CORS step in `self-hosting.mdx` and `production-readiness.mdx`, and the plugin README. Two doc lines called `OS_TRUSTED_ORIGINS` a CORS list. That was never what the transport read, and under the new default it would send an operator to the wrong variable, so both lines are corrected.

## Contract

Every input whose answer changes. "Admitted" means the origin is echoed in `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`.

| Input | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No list, credentials on (the default), not a development boot | every origin admitted, with credentials | no cross-origin caller admitted |
| No list, credentials on, development boot | every origin admitted, with credentials | loopback origins only, with credentials |
| No list, `OS_CORS_CREDENTIALS=false`, not a development boot | every origin admitted, without credentials | no cross-origin caller admitted |
| No list, `OS_CORS_CREDENTIALS=false`, development boot | every origin admitted, without credentials | loopback origins only, without credentials |
| A list holding `*` (option or `OS_CORS_ORIGIN`, alone or among other entries), credentials on | booted; every origin admitted, with credentials | `init()` throws; the boot fails |

Unchanged:

- A list without `*`, exact origins or patterns, is admitted as before, with or without credentials. It still admits loopback origins alongside it: that is the pattern matcher's existing convenience, and this PR does not touch it.
- `*` with credentials off still boots and admits any origin without credentials.
- `cors: false`, `cors.enabled: false` and `OS_CORS_ENABLED=false` still mount nothing.
- Allowed and exposed headers, methods and max-age are unchanged. Preflights are still answered `204`, admitted or not.
- Same-origin requests are outside CORS, so the Console under `/_console` and every page the server itself serves are unaffected.
- No export, option, type or spec key moves. `HonoCorsOptions` gains TSDoc only.

## Mechanism (measured)

- The before-state was measured on `main`. The new pin file ran against `main`'s source (commit `b1bb0d25c`: `795ff708d` plus the test file only) and gave `Tests 8 failed | 4 passed (12)`. The eight failures were a foreign origin echoed back with credentials on, a loopback origin echoed outside development, and `init()` resolving for `'*'` with credentials. The four that passed are the preservation pins.
- No `serve.ts` seam was needed. The host's own origin needs no CORS admission, because a browser applies CORS to cross-origin requests only. The configured list is the one the transport already reads (`cors.origins`, else `OS_CORS_ORIGIN`). The transport reads development-ness through `isDevelopmentBoot`, and `serve` sets `NODE_ENV=development` under `--dev` before any plugin initialises. No second copy of auth's trusted-origin rules was added.
- **Consumers in this repo.** Three tests leaned on the old default, and each now names its configuration (tests only; no example and no shipped code depended on it):
  - `packages/runtime/src/http-metrics-inbound-coverage.hono.integration.test.ts` configured `'*'` with credentials, which the boot now refuses. Measured before its fix: `Plugin init failed: com.objectstack.server.hono` and 1 failed of 27. It now names the origin its preflight carries.
  - `packages/qa/http-conformance/src/hono-approvals-act.conformance.test.ts` and `hono-webhooks-redeliver.conformance.test.ts` are door-parity pins, and they compared the two doors' CORS headers by accident. Both doors now run with `cors: false`, as the suite's other parity pins already do.
  - Every other test that boots `HonoServerPlugin` with CORS on drives it from a non-browser client (Node's fetch or Hono's `app.request`), and neither enforces CORS. The only assertions on `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` in this repo are `@objectstack/hono`'s own, for its own default (see Acceptance notes). `examples/embed-objectql` mounts no HTTP server. The showcase e2e runs same-origin under `--dev`. objectui's console reaches the API same-origin: through its Vite `/api` proxy in dev, and with `VITE_SERVER_URL` empty in both `.env` files (read-only, `../objectui` at `cd4623d06`).

## Tests

All runs below are on `f7cb52d15`, the head this PR opens with, unless a line names another commit.

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-hono-server exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/cors-default-admission.test.ts`: 12/12 passed. On `main`'s source the same file gave 8 failed and 4 passed, as above. The pins, by what they assert:
  1. With no origin list, a foreign origin and (outside development) a loopback origin get no `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`, on a request and on a preflight, and the request itself is still answered.
  2. A configured origin, by option or by `OS_CORS_ORIGIN`, is admitted with credentials, and an unlisted one is not.
  3. The default admits loopback origins when `NODE_ENV` is `development`, not when it is unset or `test`.
  4. `'*'` with credentials is refused in `init()` from every source, and the kernel's bootstrap rethrows it. `'*'` without credentials boots.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-hono-server test`: 35 files, 434 tests passed.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-hono-server typecheck`: exit 0. The test layer compiles, and `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFiles` lists the new file.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/http-conformance exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2`: the whole suite, 18 files and 228 tests, passed.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2` on `http-metrics-inbound-coverage.hono.integration.test.ts` and `dispatcher-plugin.rate-limit.integration.test.ts`: 2 files, 35 tests passed.
- Consumers of the default through the built `dist/`, all green. They were measured on the tree committed as `8c038d76d`, before the last merge of `main`, which touched none of these paths:
  - the twelve `@objectstack/runtime` test files that boot `HonoServerPlugin` with CORS on: 123 tests;
  - the six `@objectstack/client` files that do: 30 tests.

## Gates

- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` derived 98 families for this diff at `f7cb52d15`. All 98 ran, each exit 0. `--ran` reconciliation: `98 derived, 98 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN`. Among them:
  - `check:adr-0087-registration --base origin/main`: one declared-breaking changeset, `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`;
  - `check:changeset-no-major`, `check:doc-anchors`, `check:doc-authoring`, `check:doc-security-posture`, `check:nul-bytes`, `check:published-files`;
  - `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:type-check-coverage` and `check:type-check-debt`.
- `pnpm lint` on `f7cb52d15`: exit 0.
- CI check-runs: pending at the time of writing.

## Changeset

`.changeset/24738-cors-default-no-cross-origin-caller.md` bumps `@objectstack/plugin-hono-server` as `minor` (the package is in the `fixed` group, pre-release `next`). It is marked **BREAKING**: an accept-set narrowing shipped as `minor` under the launch-window convention, the same form the narrowing changesets already on `main` use (for example `24341-extend-default-row-scope-refused.md`). It carries the `Clause-②` line, the ADR-0087 disposition and what an operator does. `check-changeset-no-major` forbids `major`. Whether this enters 18.0.0 is the maintainer's call (triage), and this PR does not decide it.

## Acceptance notes

- **Sibling default, not changed here.** `@objectstack/hono`'s `createHonoApp` (`packages/adapters/hono/src/index.ts`, its CORS block) carries the same default. It sits outside this card's file surface, so it is handed to the seat to file, not widened into this PR. `HARDENING.md` now tells a host composing it to name its origins explicitly.
- **Loopback with a configured list.** A configured list admits loopback origins in every mode (`matchOriginPattern`). The card's "localhost in dev only" is scoped to the default, so this is reported, not changed.
- **Held-off doc line.** `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx` (about `:523`) still calls `OS_TRUSTED_ORIGINS` "(CORS)". PR #24681 holds that file, so whichever lands second should correct it.
- **Spec default.** `CorsConfigSchema` in spec (`shared/http.zod.ts`) declares `origins` default `'*'` with `credentials` default `false`. The transport does not read it (spec lane, held off). The future `server.cors` admission should carry this default.
- **What the refusal covers.** It covers a literal `*` entry. A degenerate pattern such as `https://*` is not refused.
- **`HARDENING.md` ordering.** #24740 rewrites other sections of the same file. Triage asks the two to land serially.
